stories.title: Kiev not to be able to use SCALP missiles effectively without US’ approval — expert
stories.summary: Security and defense analyst Michael Clarke noted that SCALP depended on MALD missiles manufactured by the US corporation Raytheon
article_sentences: LONDON, August 24.

The transfer of classified data for the production of SCALP cruise missiles to Kiev will require the United States’ approval, otherwise their use can hardly be effective, Sky News security and defense analyst Michael Clarke said, commenting on UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s relevant statement.
"The reason it's quite hard for the other side to pick [the missile] up is it hugs the ground, and that ground radar, that terrain-following mapping, comes from American intelligence," he said.
He also noted that SCALP depends on MALD missiles manufactured by the US corporation Raytheon.
Such missiles are a miniature decoy which is typically launched above a main missile and can imitate the flight of aircraft or missiles, generating radar signals and overloading air defense systems.
"So in two critical ways...
you need the United States' cooperation, which is not to say the Ukrainians couldn't use it without that [SCALP], but it wouldn't be nearly as effective," Clarke added.
Commenting on the UK prime minister’s statement, Russian presidential press secretary Dmitry Peskov said that Britain is participating in the war against Russia on Kiev’s side.

stories.title: Japan’s beaches are emptying out – and vanishing
stories.summary: Japan's beaches face an existential crisis over changing lifestyles and sand erosion
article_sentences: Japan’s beaches are shrinking and closing due to severe erosion and declining visitor numbers, with many local authorities halting official beach openings for safety reasons.
Environmental damage from post-war industrialisation and climate change has disrupted natural sand replenishment, causing significant beach loss and accelerating coastline retreat.
Efforts like beach nourishment are costly and temporary, forcing some cities to treat sand replenishment as ongoing maintenance to preserve coastal culture and communities.
A beach fittingly dubbed “Ibaraki’s Gold Coast” for its sweeping, unobstructed views of the Pacific Ocean and pristine sand is now a shadow of its former self.

The Otake Coast Hokota Swimming Beach, a crescent of sand spanning 1km in Ibaraki prefecture, north-east of Tokyo, traditionally drew tens of thousands of swimmers, sunbathers and surfers every summer.

Yet in 2026, for the second time in three years, the Hokota city authorities decided against opening the beloved local landmark for the official beach season, citing “ongoing severe erosion of the sandy beaches and damage to seawall blocks”.

What was once a welcoming broad stretch of glistening sand – where surfers lingered until twilight, beachgoers lazed under parasols and children built sandcastles – has been reduced to a threadbare, modest sliver of sand.
The malaise that is afflicting Otake Beach is seen elsewhere in Japan, an archipelago of over 14,000 islands where the people’s cultural identity has long been closely bound to the ocean.
This relationship is immortalised in Japanese artist Katsushika Hokusai’s iconic ukiyo-e woodblock prints, particularly the Great Wave of Kanagawa.
It is also commemorated during umi-biraki, the modern-day rituals where Shinto priests bless the waves at public beaches to officially launch the swimming season.
Japan even has a national public holiday, Marine Day, celebrated on the third Monday of July, when the people pay homage to the sea’s bounty and take part in the therapeutic ritual of ocean bathing.
Yet the country is now experiencing a bittersweet estrangement from the seas.

stories.title: HK actor Mat Yeung’s restaurant temporarily closed by city council 10 days after opening
stories.summary: The authorities discovered that its kitchen was occupying part of a public space.
article_sentences: Hong Kong actor Mat Yeung’s roast meat restaurant in Selangor has been temporarily shut down by the Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ), just 10 days after opening its doors officially.
A closure notice was posted outside the SS2 premises on Aug 24, stating that the restaurant was required to cease operations from 1pm that day.
The notice cited alleged breaches involving the restaurant’s licence and use of the premises.
In a statement on social media, the restaurant confirmed the temporary closure and apologised to customers for any inconvenience caused.
It said the action followed the authorities’ discovery that its kitchen was occupying part of a public space.
“Following the authorities’ instructions, we will close for two days to make the necessary adjustments before resuming normal operations on Aug 26,” the statement said.
Yeung also acknowledged the temporary closure in an interview with Sing Tao Headline, saying local authorities discovered the restaurant had placed some items in the back alley.
“Perhaps we had too many things after the opening, so some of them were placed at the back.
The authorities said that was not allowed and asked us to move everything back to the warehouse.
We should be able to resume business the day after tomorrow,” the 45-year-old said.
Yeung opened his Hong Kong-style roast meat restaurant on Aug 14.
The TVB star previously told local media that opening a traditional roast meat restaurant had long been one of his dreams.
